## Motivation

Add prefix-only encoder Prefill for DeepSeek-V4.1 PD disaggregation. For an effective input of N tokens, Prefill computes [0, max(0, N−128)); Decode continues the final window with the encoder SWA history and compressor state from Prefill. The intended numerical reference is same-head collocated decoder bounded replay. GPU parity and performance validation of this protocol are still pending.

Closes #39963.

## Modifications

- Add `--dsv41-encoder-only-prefill` to both roles, validated against the official text-only 40-layer topology, KV sources `[2,8,14,20]` and 128-token window.
- Keep full layers 0–19 and layer 20's global KV/Indexer producer on Prefill; omit decoder weights, final norm, LM head and draft model. The resident layer range also limits Prefill KV allocation to 21 layers.
- Stop Prefill admission/chunking at S=max(0,N−128), preserving the original input for bootstrap, accounting and Engram history. For S=0, complete bootstrap and send metadata without allocating a Prefill KV row or running the model.
- Transfer prefix Main-KV/Indexer-K, the last encoder SWA window for layers 0–19, and the pending ratio-2 pair. Register states by layer identity; omit layers 20–39 SWA. Transfer one pair rather than an entire ring so Decode-local DSpark can use a wider ring.
- Decode reuses preallocated slots and performs a normal [S,N) extend: encoder layers read transferred SWA without a floor; layers 20–39 retain the upstream bounded-replay floor at S. Tail compression writes Main-KV/Indexer-K normally. Retain enough paged SWA for both the incoming history and the tail.
- Preserve cache accounting, cancellation, overlap ordering, priority/FIFO admission and rebootstrap token restoration. Keep ordinary non-PD encoder replay unchanged. The new mode uses paged SWA directly without enabling legacy encoder replay. Reuse common Prefill result handling and retain the shared P/D/router E2E fixture; unit-test changes are deferred.

Implementation envelope: CUDA/text-only DeepSeek-V4.1, matching TP/page size/KV dtype/layout, PP1, Mooncake, `dsv4` attention, `flashinfer_mxfp4` MoE, paged SWA and Prefill CUDA Graph disabled. The E2E fixture uses page 256/chunk 8192. Unsupported modes include DP/CP, LoRA, multimodal, mixed chunking, HiSparse, unified memory and KV checksum (its shared state-index checksum does not represent the two state components). Requests currently reject all logprobs. Decode-local DSpark remains supported by the protocol; GPU validation is pending.

## Accuracy Tests

Candidate code revision: `e9c0452b73c0172f97e346d056e74039062262cf`, based on upstream `a90e9c5dd8973cdb84af4ff6154c7b4958083b31`. All 17 unit-test file changes from this PR have been removed (three added files deleted; 14 existing files restored to the base). Unit-test selection is deferred; the shared GPU E2E fixture remains.

CPU checks on 2026-10-19, Python 3.12 / Torch 2.14.1+cpu, GPUs hidden:

- **18 unchanged upstream test files passed: 428 tests + 302 subtests.** These cover ordinary PD transfer/queues, abort and result cleanup, scheduling, compressed pools, bounded replay and model boundaries. They do not establish correctness of the new prefix-transfer protocol.
- The unchanged `test_batch_result_processor_spec_grammar.py` passes **8 tests + 9 subtests** after publishing a default runtime configuration. Its standalone command without that initialization still fails two handoff cases because the fixture has no published `disagg` namespace. This setup gap remains for the deferred test review; no fixture edits or production fallback were added.
- Startup-resolution smoke passed for both roles with legacy encoder replay disabled and Decode bounded replay enabled. Metadata-only completion records zero forward duration and preserves queue time.
- Changed-file pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed. The existing E2E file collects three cases; GPU execution was not attempted.

The existing `test/registered/e2e/disaggregation/test_dsv41_encoder_only_prefill.py` shares one TP4+TP4 P/D/router fixture across first handoff/cache accounting (127/128/129/255/256/257/8192/8193 tokens), concurrent handoff during Decode, and retract-pause/flush/resume. This revision did not allocate GPU resources or manually trigger upstream CI; execution needs a prepared eight-B300 runner.

Thanks @HanHan009527! I’ve partially ported this PR to SM120. The Prefill side is working in my local tests, and I’m currently debugging Decode.

I’d be happy to contribute the SM120 fixes and validation. Which revision should I align with, and would you prefer a PR to your branch or a separate upstream PR?

@HanHan009527 Thanks for driving this. I'm working on supporting this feature from NVIDIA's side and would like to collaborate. I'd like to suggest one design change before more is built on the current handoff. 

[Following description is mostly written by claude code. The tldr is we should only compute up to tokens N-128 on the encoder/prefill worker, and we need to also pass the encoder SWA for last 128 tokens to the decode worker]
                                                                   
It seems like in the current design, decode's layers 0–19 are approximate. Every layer reads its own 128-token SWA window. Decode currently receives only Main-KV/Indexer-K, so when it replays [N−128, N) through L0–19, those layers have no SWA history before N−128. Their outputs feed L20–39, so the error from bounded replay hits both halves of the model. Collocated `--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` only truncates L20–39. So the current PD output is not equivalent to the collocated path, and nothing can be parity-tested against it. GSM8K at this sample size (p=0.109) can't detect a gap like this.                                                   

I'd instead propose the following approach (which follows what was shipped in NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#19727 as `bounded_replay_on_generation`):
1. Prefill processes only `[0, max(0, N−128))` through L0–19 plus the L20 KV/indexer path. For N ≤ 128 it skips the forward, as the RFC describes.                                               
2. Transfer Main-KV + Indexer-K for that prefix, **plus L0–19 SWA for the last 128 prefix positions** and the ratio-2 compressor state at the boundary. L20–39 SWA is not transferred. This is about 1.5 MB per request.
3. Decode runs the tail [N−128, N) through all 40 layers as it does today, but:
     - L0–19 read the transferred SWA with no floor, so the encoder half is **exact**, exactly like the next chunk of a chunked prefill;                                                         
     - L20–39 are floored at N−128, the same as collocated decoder bounded replay;
     - the tail writes its own Main-KV/Indexer-K for [N−128, N), instead of the cache-only/state-only rebuild.
                                                                   
This makes the PD output match collocated decoder bounded replay, so we can gate on logprob/KL parity against it. It also removes the duplicated L0–19 compute on [N−128, N). Most of the decode-side replay and scheduling work in this PR carries over unchanged.
  
**Question on the current code:** on decode, the request window is disabled and paged SWA is used. As far as I can tell, the `swa_replay_start` floor in `make_core_attn_metadata` is only applied in the request-window branch, and the main `init_forward_metadata_prefill` call doesn't pass one. If so, L0–19 tail rows may read SWA slots for positions < N−128 that were never written on decode. Could you confirm? Poisoning decode's SWA pool with NaN at startup would show it quickly. I may be misreading. The proposal above makes this moot for L0–19, but L20–39 still need the floor.
                                                                   
Happy to help implement this, either as PRs against your branch or as a separate upstream PR, whichever you prefer. @zooeyQAQ, this changes the transfer payload and the decode attention metadata, so it may be worth syncing before you go deep on the SM120 decode path.

@HanHan009527 Thanks for driving this. I'm working on supporting this feature from NVIDIA's side and would like to collaborate. I'd like to suggest one design change before more is built on the current handoff. 

[Following description is mostly written by claude code. The tldr is we should only compute up to tokens N-128 on the encoder/prefill worker, and we need to also pass the encoder SWA for last 128 tokens to the decode worker]
                                                                   
It seems like in the current design, decode's layers 0–19 are approximate. Every layer reads its own 128-token SWA window. Decode currently receives only Main-KV/Indexer-K, so when it replays [N−128, N) through L0–19, those layers have no SWA history before N−128. Their outputs feed L20–39, so the error from bounded replay hits both halves of the model. Collocated `--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` only truncates L20–39. So the current PD output is not equivalent to the collocated path, and nothing can be parity-tested against it. GSM8K at this sample size (p=0.109) can't detect a gap like this.                                                   

I'd instead propose the following approach (which follows what was shipped in NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#19727 as `bounded_replay_on_generation`):
1. Prefill processes only `[0, max(0, N−128))` through L0–19 plus the L20 KV/indexer path. For N ≤ 128 it skips the forward, as the RFC describes.                                               
2. Transfer Main-KV + Indexer-K for that prefix, **plus L0–19 SWA for the last 128 prefix positions** and the ratio-2 compressor state at the boundary. L20–39 SWA is not transferred. This is about 1.5 MB per request.
3. Decode runs the tail [N−128, N) through all 40 layers as it does today, but:
